- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >10%), model often overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 3–7% in the following 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days moving toward historical mean), model tends to hold too high; adjust downward by 1–3% per day.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven volatility; use sentiment history to weight recent days (last 5–7) more heavily in smoothing.  
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often misreads trend; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule — adjust forecast midpoint by ±3% based on sentiment direction change.
